## Impact analysis: adding a job kind to the scheduler's cadence table

**Source files that must change:**
- `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts` — `CADENCE_MINUTES` (L13-21) is the cadence table itself; a new entry goes here.
- `src/server/jobs/queue.ts` — `CADENCE_MINUTES` is typed `Readonly<Record<JobKind, number>>`, so the new kind must first be added to the `JobKind` union (L16-23); the `runHandler()` switch (L124-162) also needs a new `case` or the queued job silently no-ops when drained.

**Documents that must change** (each contains a literal, hand-maintained enumeration of the cadence table's contents that would become incomplete/wrong, as opposed to files that only mention the job system in passing or are auto-generated):
- `docs/design/background-jobs.md` — DES-060 states "seven `JobKind`s" and spells out the cadence values in prose; DES-061 has a full per-kind table (kind/file/trigger/description) and the purpose section names all seven kinds explicitly.
- `docs/ops/runbook-scheduler-and-queue.md` — has its own `| job kind | CADENCE_MINUTES | plain English |` table "straight from `scheduler.ts`" plus a "walks the seven `JobKind` values" statement.
- `docs/ops/index.md` — has a second cadence table (`job kind | cadence (minutes) | primary owner | runbook`) and a "Glossary of job kinds" section that lists and describes all seven kinds by name.

I excluded `docs/traceability.md` (explicitly documented as generated, not hand-maintained) and other files that only mention "the seven job kinds" in passing (`docs/index.md`, `docs/design/index.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-016-interval-scheduler.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-018-webhook-retry-policy.md`, `docs/requirements/billing-and-plan-limits.md`, `docs/glossary.md`) since they don't carry per-kind cadence data that goes structurally wrong, just an aside that would read as slightly dated.

ANSWER: src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts, src/server/jobs/queue.ts, docs/design/background-jobs.md, docs/ops/runbook-scheduler-and-queue.md, docs/ops/index.md
